{{nihongo|'''Ena Shrine'''|恵那神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Nakatsugawa|ar|ناكاتسوغاوا غيفو|azb|ناکاتسوقاوا، قیفو|ce|Накацугава|ceb|Nakatsugawa|de|Nakatsugawa|es|Nakatsugawa|fa|ناکاتسوگاوا، گیفو|fi|Nakatsugawa|fr|Nakatsugawa|gl|Nakatsugawa|id|Nakatsugawa|it|Nakatsugawa|ja|中津川市|ko|나카쓰가와시|mg|Nakatsugawa|ms|Nakatsugawa|mzn|ناکاتسوگاوا، گیفو|nl|Nakatsugawa|pl|Nakatsugawa|pt|Nakatsugawa|ro|Nakatsugawa|ru|Накацугава|simple|Nakatsugawa|su|Nakatsugawa, Gifu|sv|Nakatsugawa|tg|Накатсугава|th|นากัตสึงาวะ|tl|Nakatsugawa, Gifu|tr|Nakatsugawa|tt|Накацугава|uk|Накацуґава|ur|ناکاٹسوگاوا|vi|Nakatsugawa, Gifu|war|Nakatsugawa, Gifu|zh|中津川市|zh_classical|中津川市|zh_min_nan|Nakatugawa-chhī|zh_yue|中津川|qid=Q844052}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. The Front Shrine is located at Shōgane, Kaore, Nakatsugawa City, and the Inner Shrine is located at the summit of Mount Ena. {{nihongo|'''Ena Shrine'''|恵那神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

== Annual festivals ==
*At the main shrine festival held every year on September 29, {{ill|Ena Bunraku|Q11492450|qid=Q11492450}} is dedicated. Ena Bunraku is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Gifu Prefecture<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/mumin/nakatugawasi/enabunnraku.html |title=Ena Bunraku |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2012-10-16}}
</ref>.

== History ==
The date of establishment is unknown. {{ill|Mount Ena|arz|جبل مونت انا|ceb|Ena-san|de|Ena (Berg)|fr|Mont Ena|ja|恵那山|lld|Mont Ena|ml|എന പർവ്വതം|my|အဲနတောင်|pl|Ena (góra)|pnb|ٹلہ اینا|vi|Núi Ena|zh|惠那山|qid=Q1339920}} is said to be the place where {{ill|Izanami|ar|إزانامي|az|İzanami|bcl|Izanami|bs|Izanami|ca|Izanami|da|Izanami|el|Ιζανάμι|eo|Izanami|es|Izanami|fa|ایزانامی|fi|Izanami|fr|Izanami|he|איזאנמי|hr|Izanami|hu|Izanami|hy|Իզանամի|id|Izanami|it|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|ko|이자나미|mk|Изанами|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯃꯤ|pt|Izanami|rsk|Изанами|ru|Идзанами|simple|Izanami|sl|Izanami|sr|Изанами|sv|Izanami|ta|இசநமி|th|อิซานามิ|tl|Izanami|tr|Izanami|uk|Ідзанамі|zh|伊邪那美|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}} enshrined the placenta (ena, meaning umbilical cord) when she gave birth to {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, and in the past Mount Ena itself was regarded as the sacred object of worship.

With Mount Ena at the center, Ena Shrine lies to the west and {{ill|Achi Shrine (Achi Village)|Q11657447|qid=Q11657447|lt=Achi Shrine}} lies to the east.

Later, through {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} (the syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism), it also came to be called Ena Gongen.

In the “Mino Province Jinmyōchō,” compiled after the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, seven shrines of Ena District are listed: the shrine at the summit of Mount Ena is recorded as '''Ena Shrine''', and the shrine at Kaore, Nakatsugawa City is recorded as '''Kajo Myōjin'''.

At the summit of Mount Ena, the following subsidiary shrines are enshrined: Katsuragi Shrine (Hitokotonushi-no-Mikoto), Fuji Shrine (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Kami), Kumano Shrine (Hayatama-no-O-Mikoto), Shinmei Shrine (Amaterasu Ōmikami and Toyouke Ōmikami), Tsurugi Shrine (Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto), and Ichinomiya Shrine (Sarutahiko-no-Kami).

Formerly, near the village shrine at the foot of the mountain there was also the {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}} temple {{ill|Sōsen-ji|Q118391408|qid=Q118391408|lt=Sōsen-ji}}, and many buildings stood there, but it is said that when {{ill|Kiso Yoshimasa|Q6416834|qid=Q6416834|lt=Kiso Yoshimasa}}, acting on orders from {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|Q662482|qid=Q662482}}, captured {{ill|Adera Castle|Q11657387|qid=Q11657387}} in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}), the temple and buildings were destroyed<ref>Misakagoe-ki</ref>.

Records remain of a ridge tag stating “Reconstruction of all seven shrines” in Tenshō 4 (1576)<ref>Nakagawa Kyūki (Hōra-zasshi ryakusō)</ref>.

Originally, the summit of Mount Ena was the main shrine and the foot of the mountain was the front shrine, but in {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} 6 ({{ill|1620|Q6810|qid=Q6810}}), when the front shrine was newly rebuilt, the main shrine was changed to the inner shrine and the front shrine became the main shrine.

In {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} 4 ({{ill|1767|Q7672|qid=Q7672}}), the ascetic {{ill|Kakumei|Q135984112|qid=Q135984112|lt=Kakumei}} of {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}} undertook a 17-day fasting practice on Mount Ena.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 4 ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1871}}), it became the general tutelary shrine of {{ill|Ena District, Gifu|ca|Ena|fa|ناحیه انا، گیفو|fr|District d'Ena|ja|恵那郡|qid=Q3030924}} and was revered.

In Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|ab|1873|af|1873|als|1873|am|1873 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1873|ar|1873|ary|1873|arz|1873|ast|1873|avk|1873|az|1873|azb|۱۸۷۳ (میلادی)|ba|1873 йыл|ban|1873|bar|1873|bat_smg|1873|bcl|1873|be|1873|be_x_old|1873|bg|1873|bn|১৮৭৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৩|br|1873|bs|1873.|ca|1873|cdo|1873 nièng|ce|1873 шо|ceb|1873|ckb|١٨٧٣|crh|1873|cs|1873|csb|1873|cv|1873|cy|1873|da|1873|de|1873|diq|1873|el|1873|eml|1873|eo|1873|es|1873|et|1873|eu|1873|fa|۱۸۷۳|fi|1873|fiu_vro|1873|fo|1873|fr|1873|frp|1873|frr|1873|fur|1873|fy|1873|ga|1873|gan|1873年|gcr|1873|gd|1873|gl|1873|gv|1873|he|1873|hi|१८७३|hif|1873|hr|1873.|hsb|1873|ht|1873 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1873|hy|1873|hyw|1873 թուական|ia|1873|id|1873|ilo|1873|inh|1873 шу|io|1873|is|1873|it|1873|ja|1873年|jv|1873|ka|1873|kaa|1873|kk|1873 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೩|ko|1873년|krc|1873 джыл|ku|1873|kv|1873-ӧд во|la|1873|lb|1873|lez|1873 йис|li|1873|lij|1873|lmo|1873|lt|1873 m.|lv|1873. gads|mai|१८७३|map_bms|1873|mdf|1873|mg|1873|mhr|1873|mi|1873|min|1873|mk|1873|ml|1873|mr|इ.स. १८७३|mrj|1873 и|ms|1873|my|၁၈၇၃|myv|1873 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۳|nah|1873|nap|1873|nds|1873|nds_nl|1873|new|ई सं १८७३|nl|1873|nn|1873|no|1873|nrm|1873|nso|1873|oc|1873|olo|1873|or|୧୮୭୩|os|1873-æм аз|pa|1873|pl|1873|pnb|1873|pt|1873|qu|1873|ro|1873|ru|1873 год|rue|1873|sa|१८७३|sah|1873 сыл|sc|1873|scn|1873|sd|1873ع|se|1873|sh|1873.|shn|1873|si|1873|simple|1873|sk|1873|sl|1873|smn|1873|sq|1873|sr|1873|stq|1873|su|1873|sv|1873|sw|1873|szl|1873|ta|1873|te|1873|tg|Соли 1873|th|พ.ศ. 2416|tk|1873|tl|1873|tly|1873|tr|1873|tt|1873 ел|udm|1873 ар|ug|1873 - يىلى|uk|1873|ur|1873ء|uz|1873|vec|1873|vi|1873|vls|1873|vo|1873|wa|1873|war|1873|wuu|1873年|xmf|1873|yi|1873|za|1873 nienz|zea|1873|zh|1873年|zh_classical|一八七三年|zh_min_nan|1873 nî|zh_yue|1873年|qid=Q7757}}), it became the village shrine of six villages in Ena District ({{ill|Nakatsu|Q11366500|qid=Q11366500|lt=Nakatsugawa Village}}, {{ill|Tegano|Q22125621|qid=Q22125621}}, {{ill|Komanba|Q22126184|qid=Q22126184|lt=Koma-ba Village}}, {{ill|Sendanbayashi|Q22131707|qid=Q22131707}}, {{ill|Nasubigawa|Q22126369|qid=Q22126369}}, {{ill|Ochiai|Q11620598|qid=Q11620598|lt=Ochiai Village}}), and in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 14 ({{ill|1925|Q18107|qid=Q18107}}) it became a prefectural shrine.

On March 1, {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 28 ({{ill|1953|Q18585|qid=Q18585}}), it received designation from the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines as a shrine designated for visits by the head of the prefectural association ({{ill|Kinpei-sha|ja|金幣社|qid=Q119929592}}) (Designation No. Kin-21) {{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=141}}.

== Designated cultural properties ==
== Important Cultural Property of Gifu Prefecture ==
*[https://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/page/6162.html Tachi, inscription: Sadatsuna]<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/kougeihin/nakatugawasi/tachimeisadatuna.html |title=Tachi, inscription: Sadatsuna |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-05-13}}</ref>
Length 76.2 cm; curvature 3.6 cm; Heian period; designated on August 5, {{ill|1969|Q2485|qid=Q2485}}.

The swordsmith Sadatsuna, famed for his powerful blades, is said to have lived during the {{ill|Kankō|az|Kanko erası|de|Kankō|fa|کانکو|fr|Ère Kankō|ia|Kanko|id|Kankō|ja|寛弘|ko|간코|ru|Канко|simple|Kankō|sr|Канко|tr|Kankō|uk|Канко|zh|寬弘|zh_yue|寬弘|qid=Q2736722}} era, and according to the “Ena Shrine Chronicle,” it was dedicated by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|Q1139202|qid=Q1139202|lt=Kiso Yoshinaka}}.

It is currently preserved at the {{ill|Naegi Tōyama Historical Museum|Q48747312|qid=Q48747312}}.

== Natural Monument of Gifu Prefecture ==
*[https://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/page/7393.html Married cedars of Ena Shrine]
The pair of cedars in front of the main shrine were designated as a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} of Gifu Prefecture on September 14, {{ill|1966|Q2649|qid=Q2649}}. The left “husband” cedar has a trunk circumference of 6.29 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m}} and a height of 47 m; the right “wife” cedar has a trunk circumference of 5.48 m and a height of 46 m. Their estimated age is 600 to 800 years, and they are in vigorous condition<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.city.nakatsugawa.gifu.jp/wiki/%E6%81%B5%E9%82%A3%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%E3%81%AE%E5%A4%AB%E5%A9%A6%E3%82%B9%E3%82%AE |title=Married Cedars of Ena Shrine
 |publisher=Nakatsugawa City |date=2009-01-28 |accessdate=2011-07-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|date=|url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/tenki/nakatigawasi/enajinnjya.html|title=Married Cedars of Ena Shrine|publisher=Gifu Prefecture|accessdate=2012-10-16|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140716233352/http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/tenki/nakatigawasi/enajinnjya.html|archivedate=2014-07-16|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2017-10}}</ref>.

== Transportation ==
*From Nakatsugawa Station Bus Terminal ({{ill|Chūō Main Line|Q1078110|qid=Q1078110}}{{ill|Nakatsugawa Station|Q5359511|qid=Q5359511}}), platform 1, take the Kawakami Line bus of {{ill|Kitaena Kotsu|Q11401729|qid=Q11401729}} bound for “{{ill|Mount Ena Weston Park|Q17219335|qid=Q17219335}},” get off at “Mount Ena Weston Park” bus stop, then walk about 45 minutes.

== Chiarai Shrine ==
About 3.2 km southwest of Ena Shrine toward {{ill|Nenoue Highlands|Q11536226|qid=Q11536226}}<ref>Nakatsugawa City, Aki 6872-1</ref> is Chiarai Shrine.

The enshrined deities are Amaterasu Ōmikami and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōyama-tsumi-no-Kami}}, enshrined together.

Originally, it stood beside the '''Chiarai Pond''', where Izanami-no-Mikoto is said to have washed and purified the placenta after giving birth to Amaterasu Ōmikami.

Chiarai Pond was said to have been a large pond with a depth of 5 m and an area of 1 ha, but in {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} 1 ({{ill|1704|Q6824|qid=Q6824}}), heavy rains caused landslides that filled it with sediment, and by the early {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} period it had become a small pond of about one tsubo; eventually the pond disappeared, and today only a stone monument marking the site remains.

It is said that after giving birth, Izanami-no-Mikoto sat on a rock to rest<ref>There is a “sitting rock” near Chiarai Pond.</ref>, felt relieved, and said, “Name this place the Village of Ease.”

Later, “Yasugi” changed to “Yasugi,” and in the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period it became {{ill|Agi|Q11657459|qid=Q11657459|lt=Agi}}.

Near the summit area of Mount Ena is {{ill|Misaka Pass|Q11588847|qid=Q11588847}}, and the origin of this place name is said to be that Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto crossed the pass to enter {{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}}.

There is also a place name called Yufunezawa at the foot of Mount Ena, which is said to have been named because water was used there for the first bath of Amaterasu Ōmikami.
